claims.statement: src/worker.py defines the Huey instance as MemoryHueyWithRegistry when settings.environment is "test" and RedisHueyWithRegistry (url=settings.redis_url) otherwise; its @huey.on_startup hook builds a worker-only svcs Registry by reusing register_services with a DatabaseSessionManager configured with NullPool (so every task's asyncio.run loop avoids pooled-engine "operation in progress" errors), assigns it to huey.svcs_registry, and @huey.on_shutdown closes that registry.

The three task modules src.account.task, src.integration.task and src.market.task are imported at the bottom of src/worker.py solely so their @huey.task/@huey.periodic_task decorators register against the shared huey instance, which is why task-registry tests can assert membership in huey._registry.

Task bodies split into three guard styles on huey.svcs_registry: critical periodic work (the daily and hourly price updates, account totals recalculation and the broker position sync) raises RuntimeError("Worker registry not initialized"); best-effort tasks (note-title generation, price-alert evaluation and alert email dispatch) return early; and _daily_fx_refresh never consults the registry at all because it needs only the shared Redis client. The first two styles then resolve their dependencies through Container(huey.svcs_registry), and the request-id-carrying tasks reset the contextvar in a finally.

The API resolves services from a registry built in lifespan_context and stored on app.state.svcs_registry, which is a different registry instance from the worker's huey.svcs_registry; the two are deliberately separate so task code never resolves from the app registry and the API never touches the worker registry.

hourly_intraday_price_update is a @huey.periodic_task(crontab(minute="0")) that, after running MarketService.update_intraday_prices_for_all_securities and logging success/failure counts, enqueues recalculate_all_account_totals_task and then check_and_dispatch_price_alerts, each inside its own try/except that only logs, so a failed enqueue of one does not abort the other or the periodic task.

Stage 2 (check_and_dispatch_price_alerts) returns early when there are no active alerts, otherwise loads all active alerts plus one bulk latest-intraday-close map, delegates the condition check to the pure AlertEvaluationService.evaluate (inclusive comparisons, missing price skips the alert), and enqueues one alert_email_dispatch_task(alert_id, run_ts) per triggered alert, logging and continuing when an individual enqueue raises.

alert_email_dispatch_task declares retries=3 and implements email-then-mark: it re-fetches the alert as an idempotency guard against duplicate dispatch, re-resolves the latest price at dispatch time, sends the email, and only then calls mark_triggered; a send failure is re-raised so Huey retries and triggered_at stays NULL so the next hourly Stage 2 run re-enqueues it.

Huey periodic schedules only fire when the consumer is started with --periodic: the dev compose worker command is `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread --periodic` (wrapped in watchfiles), while docker-compose.prod.yml omits --periodic, and a test reads docker-compose.yml to assert the flag is present as the regression guard for empty intraday price tables.

sync_account_positions_task orders its side effects: mark_sync_started in its own log-only try/except, then the sync_started event, then _do_sync_positions, then sync_finished; on any exception it logs, attempts the error email in its own try/except, publishes sync_failed, and re-raises so the Huey task is recorded as failed, while mark_sync_finished runs in a finally on every exit path.

A @huey.signal(signals.SIGNAL_INTERRUPTED) handler in src/integration/task.py inspects task.name == "sync_account_positions_task", reads task.args[0]/task.args[1], and calls mark_sync_finished via asyncio.run, so a killed worker does not leave an account stuck in the active-sync set until the TTL expires.

The broker sync task is enqueued synchronously from the request path by POST /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/sync (rate-limited 3/minute, via PositionService and IntegrationAccountApi) and once per newly imported broker account in the broker import route, both forwarding get_request_id() so worker logs correlate with the originating request.

ConnectionManager keeps a user-keyed local connection registry (dict[UserId, list[WebSocket]]) and one Redis client per running event loop in a map guarded by a threading.Lock, pruning and aclose-ing clients whose loop has closed; the FastAPI lifespan initializes it (starting the pub/sub listener in the API's main loop) and closes it on shutdown.

send_personal_message publishes json {"user_id": ..., "message": ...} to the Redis channel ws_messages, lazily initializing a publish-only client (run_listener=False) when the calling loop has no client, and falls back to _send_to_local_connections both when that initialization fails and when the publish raises, so a Redis outage degrades to same-process delivery rather than dropping the event.

The pub/sub listener subscribes to ws_messages, sends to local sockets only when client_state is WebSocketState.CONNECTED, logs and continues on a malformed payload, unsubscribes and closes the pubsub on CancelledError, and restarts itself after a 5-second sleep on any other exception.

The /api/ws endpoint authenticates with either a signed ticket (URLSafeTimedSerializer.loads with max_age=30 and salt "ws-ticket") or the auth_token cookie / sec-websocket-protocol header resolved through UserApi, and closes with WebSocket close code 1008 on every failure; tickets are single-use via SET ws-ticket-used:<sha256(ticket)> "1" NX EX 30, and the guard fails open (treats the ticket as new) when Redis raises.

The WebSocket ticket is minted by POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket, which requires the auth_token cookie (401 otherwise) and dumps {"user_id", "jti"} with salt "ws-ticket"; the frontend obtains it through authService.getWsTicket and aborts the connection with a warning rather than connecting unauthenticated when no ticket is returned.

Account-sync display state is a single Redis set, account_syncs:active:{user_id}, written by mark_sync_started (SADD plus EXPIRE settings.sync_ttl_seconds, default 300), cleared by mark_sync_finished (SREM) and read back as UUIDs by get_active_syncs (SMEMBERS); the TTL is the safety net for a worker that dies without cleanup, and the set is display state rather than a lock because duplicate syncs collapse into one member.
GET /api/v1/accounts/sync-status returns {"account_ids": [...]} for the authenticated user only and translates redis.RedisError into HTTP 503 "Sync status service unavailable".

AccountsListState hydrates sync state exactly once per connection open by reading GET /accounts/sync-status (guarded by a syncStatusHydrated flag that onclose resets), maps sync_started/sync_finished/sync_failed onto its syncingAccountIds set and syncErrors record, and reconnects after a fixed 5000 ms timeout on close.

syncAccount awaits waitForSyncFinish, an intentionally independent poll of GET /accounts/sync-status every 1500 ms with a 60000 ms deadline and a 5000 ms grace period once the backend stops reporting the account, because the WebSocket message may be lost if Redis pub/sub fails; it clears state and refetches accounts when the socket message never arrives, and reports a timeout or a request failure through syncErrors.

WsEventType declares sync_started, sync_finished, sync_failed and account_totals_updated, carried by AccountSyncMessage and AccountTotalsUpdatedMessage; the frontend enum declares only the three sync values, so an account_totals_updated payload matches no branch in AccountsListState.

recalculate_all_account_totals_task iterates every account, skips inactive ones, computes totals per account and publishes one account_totals_updated message to the account's user, isolating per-account failures so one error does not stop the remaining accounts.

generate_note_title_task is the on-demand task enqueued by the security-note create and update routes with the current request id; its async body returns early when huey.svcs_registry is absent and otherwise resolves SecurityNoteRepository and AIService to generate and persist the title.

The worker dashboard router is mounted on the backend FastAPI app at /worker/api: its huey-dashboard task routes carry dependencies=[Depends(current_user)] (401 without credentials) and its WebSocket at /worker/api/updates (and the trailing-slash variant) authenticates via the shared _check_ticket_not_replayed helper plus a salt="ws-ticket" max_age=30 payload, or via the auth_token cookie / sec-websocket-protocol token, closing with code 1008 on failure. Finding 3 of the archived architecture review — which lived in .opencode/reviews/2026-08-25-architecture.md and now lives at .ai/reviews/2026-08-25-architecture.md — that /worker/api was unauthenticated is therefore remediated in current source.

The worker dashboard API is served by the backend process, not the worker: init_worker_dashboard creates the huey-dashboard task table, stores {"huey", "redis", "manager", "db"} on app.state.huey_dashboard, optionally registers the dashboard signal handlers on the running loop and starts the dashboard's Redis pub/sub listener; close_worker_dashboard stops the listener and closes the Redis client, both called from the FastAPI lifespan, while the worker only feeds it by calling init_worker_signals in setup_worker_services and the dev worker service setting HUEY_DASHBOARD_WORKER: 1.

Test isolation for the async runtime is global: tests/conftest.py sets huey.immediate = True so tasks run synchronously without a broker, patches ConnectionManager's init_redis/close/send_personal_message/send_personal_message_sync on the class, patches src.main's dashboard init/close bindings, and the autouse fake_redis_manager fixture replaces the src.core.redis.redis_manager client with a dict-backed FakeRedis implementing set(nx=...), sadd/srem/smembers and publish — so no test requires a live Redis, a running worker, or a real socket.

daily_fx_refresh is a @huey.periodic_task(crontab(hour="17", minute="30")) in src/market/task.py whose body opens no svcs Container: it passes redis_manager.client() and an httpx.AsyncClient to refresh_fx_rates, which stores the ECB history under the fx:ecb:zip and fx:ecb:fetched_at keys that FxRateProvider reads; its periodic registration and its delegation are pinned by tests/market/test_fx.py.

Redis (settings.redis_url) carries six distinct runtime roles, none of which is a distributed lock: the Huey broker queue of RedisHueyWithRegistry, the ws_messages pub/sub channel used by the WebSocket fan-out, the account_syncs:active:{user_id} display set, the ws-ticket-used:{sha256} replay guard written with SET NX EX 30, slowapi's rate-limit storage (settings.redis_url outside ENVIRONMENT=test, memory:// in tests), and the fx:ecb:* ECB snapshot written by daily_fx_refresh; the shared redis_manager singleton and the separate per-loop client map inside ConnectionManager are two independent client pools.

RedisManager builds every loop-scoped client with socket_timeout and socket_connect_timeout defaulting to 5.0 seconds so a stalled Redis fails fast instead of blocking a task or the /health/ready probe, whereas ConnectionManager creates its per-loop pub/sub clients without those explicit timeouts.

lifespan_context shuts the async runtime down in order — close_worker_dashboard(app), then ws_manager.close(), then redis_manager.close() — so the API loop stops the dashboard listener, cancels the pub/sub listener together with its loop-keyed clients, and finally clears the shared per-loop Redis clients.

The SIGNAL_INTERRUPTED cleanup path in src/integration/task.py has no regression guard: no test dispatches the huey signal, and the sync-task tests assert only the mark_sync_started/mark_sync_finished pairing of the success and failure exit paths.
